question: What primarily distinguishes a data lake from a data warehouse?
options: A data lake can only store structured tables
A data lake stores raw data of any format (often schema-on-read); a warehouse stores structured, modeled data (schema-on-write)
A warehouse cannot run SQL queries
A data lake requires more expensive storage than a warehouse
explanation: Data lakes hold raw data in many formats with schema applied at read time; warehouses hold curated, structured data with schema enforced at write time.

question: What is a lakehouse architecture?
options: A warehouse that has been physically moved next to a lake
A lake that only stores backups of a warehouse
An OLTP database bolted onto object storage
A platform that combines data-lake storage flexibility with warehouse-style management, ACID transactions, and SQL performance
explanation: A lakehouse adds warehouse features (ACID transactions, schema management, performant SQL) directly on top of low-cost data-lake storage via open table formats.

question: Which open table format is commonly associated with enabling ACID transactions on a data lake to build a lakehouse?
options: Delta Lake / Apache Iceberg
CSV
Plain gzip
JSON Lines
explanation: Open table formats like Delta Lake, Apache Iceberg, and Hudi add transactions, schema evolution, and metadata to files in object storage, enabling lakehouses.

question: A team wants cheap storage of raw, unstructured logs AND governed, high-performance SQL analytics on curated data, without maintaining two separate systems. Which platform pattern fits best?
options: A pure OLTP relational database
A traditional on-premise warehouse only
A lakehouse
A key-value cache
explanation: The lakehouse pattern targets exactly this need: raw cheap storage plus governed, performant analytics on one platform, avoiding separate lake and warehouse silos.

question: Which statement about schema-on-read vs schema-on-write is correct?
options: Schema-on-read validates structure at load time
Both approaches always reject malformed data before storage
Schema-on-write is used only by data lakes
Schema-on-write (warehouse) validates structure at load time; schema-on-read (lake) interprets structure at query time
explanation: Warehouses enforce schema when data is written (schema-on-write); lakes store raw data and apply schema when it is read (schema-on-read), offering flexibility.
